project_name: Wodgina Lithium Project power (52 MW permanent gas station plus 17 MW interim diesel variation)
selection_note: Hindsight-selected development case (not a sealed holdout), taken from an unverified lead. Target is the 17 MW temporary-diesel variation to Contract Power's EPC contract. Marked INCOMPLETE because the original award of the 52 MW permanent gas station to Contract Power predates this variation and its announcement was not found, so the true first procurement signal and a longer lead time cannot be established.

lead_time.note: INCOMPLETE, so no lead time is stated. Indicative only: s1/s2 (ASX 15/06/2018 16:08 +10:00) to the variation release (ASX 21/08/2018 11:39 +10:00) is about 66.8 days, but the first procurement (the 52 MW gas-station award to Contract Power) pre-dates both, and s1 already says the station was designed and under construction, so the interval is not a lead time to procurement.

blockers: First procurement missing: the target capture itself refers to a 'previously announced award ... of a contract to build a 52MW gas fired power station'; that award announcement was not located (Pacific Energy / PEA announcement list returned nothing). It likely pre-dates s1, which already says the station was designed and under construction.

The target is a variation (interim diesel on MinRes-owned assets) on an existing EPC contract, not a fresh competitive procurement; the release says MinRes' original plan was to hire interim power from a third party.
No earlier feasibility/permit signals captured for Wodgina power.
ASX release times read from ASX listing (Sydney time) via curl; listing pages not captured.
Wodgina is a JV (non-process infrastructure owned by the Wodgina JV, operated by MRL as JV Manager); MinRes is therefore not recorded as sole owner.
reviewer_checklist: Find the original Contract Power 52 MW award announcement (Pacific Energy, before 21 Aug 2018) and decide whether it should be the target.
Confirm ASX timestamps (15/06/2018 4:08 pm, 21/08/2018 11:39 am Sydney time).
Decide whether a variation order counts as a procurement of the right kind for temporary generation.
Confirm the Pacific Energy / Contract Power parent-subsidiary relation is as stated in the announcement.
target_fit_note: A variation order to an existing EPC contract to install and commission 17 MW of interim/temporary diesel power on MinRes-owned assets (MinRes chose to buy rather than hire the interim units). It is interim power but it is a variation on a contract that already existed, not a fresh competitive procurement; the first procurement (the 52 MW gas station award) is missing.
